_meta.indication: VEOZAH is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, 12-week double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, multicenter study followed by a 40-week non-controlled extension period
pivotal_trials.population: Menopausal women 40 to 65 years of age with a minimum average of 7 moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes) per day
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: mean change from baseline in frequency and severity of moderate to severe VMS at Weeks 4 and 12
pivotal_trials.n: 527 randomized to fezolinetant 30 mg, 45 mg, or placebo (VEOZAH 45 mg n=174, placebo n=175 in efficacy analysis)
pivotal_trials.result: VEOZAH 45 mg reduced VMS frequency vs placebo (Trial 1): difference -2.1 (95% CI -2.9, -1.3) at Week 4 and -2.6 (95% CI -3.4, -1.7) at Week 12, both p < 0.0011

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, 12-week double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, multicenter study followed by a 40-week non-controlled extension period
pivotal_trials.population: Menopausal women 40 to 65 years of age with a minimum average of 7 moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes) per day
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: mean change from baseline in frequency and severity of moderate to severe VMS at Weeks 4 and 12
pivotal_trials.n: 501 randomized to fezolinetant 30 mg, 45 mg, or placebo (VEOZAH 45 mg n=167, placebo n=167 in efficacy analysis)
pivotal_trials.result: VEOZAH 45 mg reduced VMS frequency vs placebo (Trial 2): difference -2.6 (95% CI -3.5, -1.6) at Week 4 and -2.5 (95% CI -3.6, -1.5) at Week 12, both p < 0.0011

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2% and > placebo) are abdominal pain (4.3% vs 2.1%), diarrhea (3.9% vs 2.6%), insomnia (3.9% vs 1.8%), back pain (3.0% vs 2.1%), hot flush (2.5% vs 1.6%), and hepatic transaminase elevation (2.3% vs 0.8%); transaminase elevations >3x ULN occurred in 2.3% on VEOZAH vs 0.9% on placebo.
target_moa: Fezolinetant is a neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor antagonist that blocks neurokinin B (NKB) binding on the KNDy neuron to modulate neuronal activity in the thermoregulatory center; it has high NK3 affinity (Ki 19.9 to 22.1 nmol/L).

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee meeting was not held because there were no considerations that would warrant a discussion.

basis.text: NDA 216578 was reviewed under a Priority Review designation, with a PDUFA Goal Date of February 22, 2023 that was extended to May 22, 2023 following a major amendment submitted January 27, 2023. Separately, Astellas notified FDA of their intent to use a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher.

citations.quote: PDUFA Goal Date	February 22, 2023 (Extended to May 22, 2023)

On March 22, 2022, Astellas notified FDA (under IND 130277) of their intent to use a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV). NDA 216578 was reviewed under a Priority Review designation with a PDUFA date of February 22, 2022. On January 27, 2023, Astellas submitted information that constituted a major amendment to this application. Thus, the goal date was extended to May 22, 2023.

summary.text: NDA 216578 for the new molecular entity fezolinetant was submitted June 22, 2022 under section 505(b) and reviewed under a Priority Review designation; it was approved May 12, 2023 as a first in class NK3 receptor antagonist without accelerated approval or a REMS.
